subject: Cross-hemisphere deep-dive: finding a shared 60–90m window
messages:
From: Tom Wallace <t.wallace@acme-systems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Li Wei <li.wei@acme-systems.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 60–90m technical deep-dive (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our architects (Li and I) would like a focused 60–90 minute session with a solutions engineer to walk through inference topology, network diagrams for Private, and observability hooks. Our team spans SF, Dublin, and Singapore so timezone overlap is tight — DST differences make it tricky.

Can your team propose 3 candidate windows over the next two weeks that take DST into account? Ideally weekdays only; we prefer early-PDT or lunchtime-UTC slots so our APAC folks aren't after 10pm local. We can be flexible on the agenda.

Attaching a one-pager on our goals.

Thanks,
Tom Wallace
Principal Cloud Architect
Acme Systems
[attachment: acme-requirements-summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wallace <t.wallace@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Li Wei <li.wei@acme-systems.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: 60–90m technical deep-dive (US/EU/APAC)

Tom — thanks, that framing helps. I ran a quick availability sweep with Marissa (SE) and Karthik (network lead) and we have an approach that usually works for tri-region deep dives: a quick "slot allocation" where participants mark strict 2–3 windows and we pick the best 60–90m overlap. To avoid DST surprises we attach a timezone matrix (see tri-region-availability-matrix.csv) showing local offsets during your proposed weeks.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached two files: a draft agenda (acme-deepdive-agenda-v1.pdf) and the availability CSV.
- Can you ask your architects to mark 2–3 preferred windows (their local time) in the CSV by EOD Wednesday?
- We'll convert to UTC, propose three candidate slots, and lock one with a calendar invite.

Quick note on DST: US/PDT shifts are earlier than EU (Ireland stays on DST but the change date differs). For the week of Jun 28 we still have DST in all regions, so offsets are stable; the risk is if we cross into late-Oct/early-Nov windows.

Marissa will drive the technical agenda; Karthik will pick the network/readiness checklist.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Tom Wallace <t.wallace@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Li Wei <li.wei@acme-systems.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:41:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 60–90m technical deep-dive (US/EU/APAC)

Folks — adding a few observations from the SE side after skimming your one-pager:
- Best technical value: 90 minutes if you want hands-on network config and a short runbook exercise.
- If 90 is tight, we can do 60 + a follow-up office hours session (30m) the next week.

My raw availability for the next two weeks (local times shown):
- Mon/Wed/Fri mornings PDT (08:00–10:30 PDT) — good for US-first windows.
- Tue/Thu 12:00–14:30 UTC (13:00–15:30 CET) — works for EU midday and APAC late evening.
- I cannot do >21:30 SGT on weekdays.

I'll pre-fill the CSV with my constraints and a few preferred UTC conversion examples so Li and Tom can mark theirs quickly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: se-deepdive-checklist.md (TEXT)]

From: Li Wei <li.wei@acme-systems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:17:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: Request: 60–90m technical deep-dive (US/EU/APAC)

Hi all — thanks for the fast turn. I updated the CSV (rows highlighted): my local constraints are 09:00–12:00 SGT and 19:00–22:30 SGT — the latter is possible but not preferred. Tom and I discussed rotating the slot if this becomes a regular series; for the initial deep-dive we prefer a single session that hits these items: architecture validation, Private deployment network checklist, and an example observability trace.

Two constraints to call out:
1) Our security reviewer needs to be looped if we discuss KMS/HSM specifics — can we keep that as a follow-on 30m?
2) If we pick a slot that is 23:00+ SGT, Li will likely join on delay and review the recording (prefer to avoid).

I left notes in the CSV and added a green highlight to a candidate window: 13:00–14:30 UTC on Wed, Jun 30 (that maps to 06:00–07:30 PDT and 21:00–22:30 SGT).

—Li
Li Wei
Principal Architect, Acme Systems

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wallace <t.wallace@acme-systems.com>, Li Wei <li.wei@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 12:58:00 +01:00
Subject: Confirmed: Wed Jun 30 13:00–14:30 UTC (Acme technical deep-dive)

Tom / Li — thanks for the updates and the CSV. Based on everyone's constraints the best single overlap is the slot Li highlighted: Wed, Jun 30, 13:00–14:30 UTC. That maps as follows:
- PDT: Wed Jun 30, 06:00–07:30 (Marissa will be online early; Mina + Karthik will dial in)
- CET/IST: Wed Jun 30, 14:00–15:30 CET (local Dublin overlap)
- SGT: Wed Jun 30, 21:00–22:30 SGT (Li will join; understand this is late)

Action items:
- I've sent the calendar invite to everyone and attached the agenda/CSV to the invite.
- Marissa will prepare a short lab exercise; Karthik will validate the network checklist.
- Security questions (KMS/HSM) will be tabled for a dedicated 30m follow-up with Acme's security reviewer — we can schedule that after the deep-dive if needed.

If anyone absolutely cannot make that slot, flag before EOD Thursday and we'll consider the secondary slot (Thu Jul 1, 12:00–13:30 UTC).

See you all on Jun 30 — thanks,

Mina Haddad
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
[attachment: acme-deepdive-agenda-v1.pdf, tri-region-availability-matrix.csv]
